sentences.zh: 她比截止日期提前一天就把音频片段发给了我们。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: Well, first off, we asked her a bunch of questions about getting to write and direct this episode, and here's what she had to say.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们问了她很多关于编写和执导这一集的问题，以下是她的回答。

sentences.en: Hey, Jenna and Angela.
sentences.zh: 嘿，珍娜和安吉拉。

sentences.en: Thanks for these incredibly thoughtful questions about Michael's last Dundies.
sentences.zh: 感谢你们提出这些关于迈克尔最后一届邓迪奖的深刻问题。

sentences.en: So I have to admit to you guys that I was feeling really vulnerable about this particular episode and revisiting it and watching it.
sentences.zh: 我得向你们承认，在重温和观看这一集时，我感到非常脆弱。

sentences.en: And I tried to pinpoint why that is, because I have nothing but joyous memories of working on the show.
sentences.zh: 我试着找出原因，因为我对这部剧只有快乐的回忆。

sentences.en: And I think the answer is because I directed this one.
sentences.zh: 我想答案是因为这一集是我执导的。

sentences.en: And I was so nervous directing the show because I loved writing for the show.
sentences.zh: 执导这部剧让我非常紧张，因为我太热爱为这部剧写剧本了。

sentences.en: And to this day, I think I've only directed two episodes of television, and they were both from The Office 16 years ago.
sentences.zh: 时至今日，我想我只执导过两集电视剧，而且都是16年前的《办公室》。

sentences.en: So I loved directing.
sentences.zh: 所以我很喜欢执导。

sentences.en: I think it was awesome that Greg and Howard let me write and direct an episode of TV.
sentences.zh: 我觉得格雷格和霍华德能让我编剧并执导一集电视剧真是太棒了。

sentences.en: In fact, it was their suggestion that I did it because I was too scared to volunteer.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这是他们的建议，因为我当时太害怕了，不敢主动请缨。

sentences.en: I think Greg chose for me to direct this episode because it was a bookend with the first Dundies episode.
sentences.zh: 我想格雷格选择让我执导这一集，是因为它与第一集《邓迪奖》首尾呼应。

sentences.en: But I don't think we ever spoke about that.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们从未谈论过这一点。

sentences.en: Greg is not, like, so sentimental that he would have been like, do you remember six years ago or seven years ago when you wrote The Dundies and now we've come full circle?
sentences.zh: 格雷格并不是那种多愁善感的人，他不会说，你还记得六七年前你写《邓迪奖》的时候吗，现在我们又回到了原点？

sentences.en: I mean, I wish he was that way, but he's just not.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我希望他是那样的人，但他真的不是。

sentences.en: It's very funny.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: I had wondered how she got assigned to this episode since she had written the first one.
sentences.zh: 我一直好奇她是怎么被分配到这一集的，毕竟她写了第一集。

sentences.en: I thought maybe it was intentional.
sentences.zh: 我以为这可能是刻意安排的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We also asked Mindy, what were some of the biggest differences between writing the first Dundies and then writing and directing this one?
sentences.zh: 我们还问了敏迪，编写第一届邓迪奖和编写并执导这一集之间最大的区别是什么？

sentences.en: Here's what she said.
sentences.zh: 她是这样说的。

sentences.en: I think the biggest thing was how much more enjoyable it was for me to have written the first Dundies than it was to write and direct this one from season seven,
sentences.zh: 我认为最大的区别在于，编写第一届邓迪奖比编写并执导第七季的这一集要愉快得多，

sentences.en: which seems crazy because I was directing Carell and Will Ferrell and, you know, obviously our amazing caSt.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很疯狂，因为我当时在执导卡瑞尔、威尔·法瑞尔，还有我们出色的演员阵容。

sentences.en: I was directing a script I had written, which is like everybody's dream is to direct their own words.
sentences.zh: 我当时在执导自己写的剧本，这可是每个人的梦想，执导自己的文字。

sentences.en: And I just remember being terrified.
sentences.zh: 但我只记得当时非常害怕。

sentences.en: Um, and I'll tell you what really terrified me and this is going to sound ridiculous, but like making sure I didn't sleep through my alarm because when you're a director,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我告诉你们什么让我真正感到害怕，这听起来很荒谬，但就是确保我不会睡过闹钟，因为当你是一名导演时，

sentences.en: you have to be on time.

sentences.zh: 这不像当演员，你可以迟到个八分钟，让发型和化妆团队帮你补救一下，然后你就像是，

sentences.en: it is such a bad look if you're not there.
sentences.zh: 如果你不在场，那看起来真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: So I was really terrified.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时真的吓坏了。

sentences.en: Um, I also had the sense that this was an episode that was, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我当时也觉得这一集，你知道，

sentences.en: sort of important in the emotional arc of the series where Michael would be leaving and it was like our beloved Steve.
sentences.zh: 在剧集的情感走向中很重要，因为迈克尔要离开了，而且那是我们深爱的史蒂夫。

sentences.en: And it was, I think that we wrote the script, you know, it with the Dundies, it's always one of those ones where you have to come up with these like jokey jokes.
sentences.zh: 我想我们写剧本的时候，你知道，关于邓迪奖，总是那种你必须想出一些玩笑梗的剧集。

sentences.en: And by jokey jokes, I mean, the names of the Dundee Awards, it's not just like a joke from the office, it's like an extra joke.
sentences.zh: 我说的玩笑梗，是指邓迪奖的奖项名称，那不仅仅是办公室里的笑话，更像是额外的笑话。

sentences.en: So it can be funny, but not like so clever.
sentences.zh: 所以它得好笑，但又不能太聪明。

sentences.en: So I remember that being challenging.
sentences.zh: 所以我记得那很有挑战性。

sentences.zh: 我是说，我能想象能去构思邓迪奖的笑话一定很有趣。

sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 你知道，他只是在做他自己擅长的事。

sentences.zh: 我觉得如果让他在那一集里出现，在情感上说不通，而且我认为强行安排德怀特在不符合角色逻辑的情况下出现，

sentences.en: I think, been a bridge too far.
sentences.zh: 我想，那会有些过火了。

sentences.en: But I did feel like emotionally, it's like what the cast, the actors, and also the characters sort of wanted to express.
sentences.zh: 但我确实觉得在情感上，这就像是演员们，以及角色们想要表达的东西。

sentences.en: And we knew that like Steve is so good when Michael's emotional.
sentences.zh: 我们知道史蒂夫在表现迈克尔的情感流露时非常出色。

sentences.en: He's like and gets touched.
sentences.zh: 他那种被触动的感觉。

sentences.en: So and it just felt like it was nearing the end.
sentences.zh: 所以，这感觉就像是临近尾声了。

sentences.en: So it needed to happen.
sentences.zh: 因此这一幕必须发生。

sentences.en: But that's my answer to that.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的回答。

sentences.en: Well, we were really curious what it must have been like to direct such a huge moment.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们真的很好奇执导这样一个重头戏是什么感觉。

sentences.en: And we asked Mindy about it.
sentences.zh: 我们问了明迪这个问题。

sentences.en: Here's what she had to say.
sentences.zh: 以下是她的回应。

sentences.en: I have to say it is so hard to direct an emotional goodbye like this.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，执导这样一场感人的告别戏真的太难了。

sentences.en: So much harder than directing a fight or even people kissing or romance and obviously harder, anything harder than comedy.
sentences.zh: 比执导打斗戏、吻戏或浪漫戏难得多，当然也比喜剧难得多。

sentences.en: Because in comedy, you kind of know when you have a scene, but in something emotional, when everyone's coming together to sing, it's very hard to give notes.
sentences.zh: 因为在喜剧里，你大概知道什么时候该拍什么，但在这种情感戏里，当大家聚在一起唱歌时，很难给出指导意见。

sentences.en: Because if it, if everyone is like feeling it so emotionally, and then you have a lot of notes, people kind of don't want to hear it.
sentences.zh: 因为如果每个人都沉浸在那种情绪中，而你又有很多意见，大家其实是不想听的。

sentences.en: They're like, don't be a drag.
sentences.zh: 他们会觉得，别扫兴啊。

sentences.en: We're all like in our feelings.
sentences.zh: 我们都沉浸在自己的情绪里。

sentences.en: And so that was, I think, one of the unique challenges of this episode.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，这是这一集独特的挑战之一。

sentences.en: I hear that.
sentences.zh: 我明白。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I also know as a cast, we were so gutted and we were in our feelings.
sentences.zh: 我也知道作为演员，我们当时都心碎了，完全沉浸在那种情绪中。

sentences.en: We were.
sentences.zh: 我们确实是。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: We got one final fan mail flurry about this scene.
sentences.zh: 我们还收到了一波关于这个场景的粉丝来信。

sentences.en: People wanted to know who wrote the song.
sentences.zh: 大家想知道是谁写的这首歌。

sentences.en: Well, Mindy wrote the lyrics and Randy said that Eve Nelson, our go-to composer, created that instrumental track that we sang along to.
sentences.zh: 嗯，歌词是明迪写的，兰迪说我们御用的作曲家伊芙·尼尔森创作了我们跟唱的那段器乐伴奏。

sentences.en: And we paid a royalty fee of $25,000 for the rights to the music.
sentences.zh: 我们为这首音乐的版权支付了25,000美元的版税。

sentences.en: And people also wanted to know, is that an accurate number of minutes that Michael would have worked in the office?
sentences.zh: 还有人想知道，那个分钟数是迈克尔在办公室工作的准确时长吗？

sentences.en: Or was it the number of minutes that Steve worked on the show?
sentences.zh: 还是史蒂夫出演这部剧的时长？

sentences.en: Well, Ange, I got out my calculator.
sentences.zh: 嗯，安吉，我拿出了计算器。

sentences.en: You did the math.
sentences.zh: 你算过了？

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So what I did was I counted all the episodes that Steve has been in.
sentences.zh: 所以我统计了史蒂夫参演的所有剧集。

sentences.en: And I assumed that we, on average, we work about 60 hours a week per episode.
sentences.zh: 我估算了一下，平均每集我们大概工作60个小时。

sentences.en: So I added all that up and did the minutes.
sentences.zh: 所以我把这些都加起来，算了一下总时长。

sentences.en: And I can tell you, it's not the number of minutes that Steve worked on the show.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你，这并不是史蒂夫在剧组工作的时长。

sentences.en: It wasn't enough minutes.
sentences.zh: 时长还不够。

sentences.en: So I'm going with the answer is it's the number of minutes Michael has worked at Dunder Mifflin.
sentences.zh: 所以我得出的结论是，这应该是迈克尔在邓德·米夫林工作的时长。

sentences.en: Because also, Michael has worked at Dunder Mifflin more than seven years, which is how long Steve worked on the show.
sentences.zh: 因为迈克尔在邓德·米夫林工作的时间也超过了七年，这正好是史蒂夫在剧组工作的时间。

sentences.en: So I hope that clears things up for everyone.
sentences.zh: 希望这能让大家清楚了。

sentences.en: It was about 10 minutes of math.
sentences.zh: 大概花了10分钟算出来的。

sentences.en: I was going to say, how long did it take you to come to your conclusion?
sentences.zh: 我正想问，你得出这个结论花了多久？

sentences.en: About 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 大概10分钟。

sentences.en: About 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 大概10分钟。

sentences.en: I mean, because I was trying to figure out a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 我是说，因为我当时在试着弄清楚很多事情。

sentences.en: I had to count episodes.
sentences.zh: 我得数一下集数。

sentences.en: I would say that's impressive.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很厉害。

sentences.en: I think it would have taken me longer than 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 要是我的话，可能得花上不止10分钟。

sentences.en: Maybe I'll get a Dundee for best calculator work.
sentences.zh: 也许我能拿个“最佳计算奖”的邓迪奖。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Next year, you'll have to see.
sentences.zh: 明年你就知道了。

sentences.en: I'm on the edge of my seat.
sentences.zh: 我拭目以待。

sentences.en: Well, the episode is going to end with a tag.
sentences.zh: 这一集最后会有一个彩蛋。

sentences.en: It's a flashback to earlier in the evening because Toby is going to win the Extreme Repulsiveness Award.
sentences.zh: 那是当晚早些时候的回忆片段，因为托比要获得“极度令人反感奖”。

sentences.en: D'Angelo is reading the cue card.
sentences.zh: 迪安杰洛在读提示卡。

sentences.en: He's like, wait, what am I?
sentences.zh: 他当时想，等等，我是什么？

sentences.en: He's like, what does this kind of mean?
sentences.zh: 他想，这到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: Toby doesn't want to go accept it.
sentences.zh: 托比不想去领奖。

sentences.en: But Oscar's like, it's his last Dundees, man.
sentences.zh: 但奥斯卡说，这是他最后一次邓迪奖了，伙计。

sentences.en: You got to play along.
sentences.zh: 你得配合一下。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And he's going to use his acceptance speech to come clean about the Scranton Strangler case for which he was a juror.
sentences.zh: 他打算利用获奖感言的机会，坦白关于斯克兰顿勒杀手案的事情，他曾是该案的陪审员。

sentences.en: And they found this person guilty and he's been given the death penalty, we find out.
sentences.zh: 我们发现他们判了那个人有罪，而且被判了死刑。

sentences.en: Toby's now not so sure that guy really did it.
sentences.zh: 托比现在不太确定那个人是否真的做了。

sentences.en: And that's how it ends.
sentences.zh: 故事就这样结束了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It almost ends like mid-sentence.
sentences.zh: 几乎是在话说到一半时结束的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like when I was watching it, I was like, wait, wait, that's it?
sentences.zh: 我看的时候就在想，等等，等等，这就完了？

sentences.en: Well, that was Michael's last Dundees.
sentences.zh: 毕竟那是迈克尔最后一次邓迪奖了。

sentences.en: I've got a few extra tidbits here for the end of the episode.
sentences.zh: 关于这一集的结尾，我还有一些额外的小花絮。

sentences.en: I didn't know where to put this information, so I'll tell it to you now.
sentences.zh: 我不知道把这些信息放在哪里合适，所以现在告诉你们。

sentences.en: This episode was originally titled Goodbye, Michael, Part 1.
sentences.zh: 这一集最初的标题是《再见，迈克尔（上）》。

sentences.en: But it was renamed and given a new release date when NBC announced that Goodbye, Michael, Steve's actual final episode, could be a supersized episode.
sentences.zh: 但当NBC宣布史蒂夫真正意义上的最后一集《再见，迈克尔》将是一集超长版时，这一集就改名并重新安排了播出日期。

sentences.en: So then this became Michael's last Dundees.
sentences.zh: 所以这一集就变成了《迈克尔的最后一次邓迪奖》。

sentences.en: But the original goodbye to Steve Carell on our show was going to be Dundees that flowed into Goodbye, Michael.
sentences.zh: 但最初对史蒂夫·卡瑞尔的告别计划是让《邓迪奖》直接衔接到《再见，迈克尔》。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: My gosh, we're literally speaking in unison.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我们简直异口同声。

sentences.en: I also thought you might be wondering what Miles McNutt thought about this episode.
sentences.zh: 我还以为你会想知道迈尔斯·麦克纳特对这一集的看法。

sentences.en: I have to tell you, from the very beginning of the episode, when you did Fast Facts, I thought for sure one of your Fast Facts was going to be what Miles McNutt thought of it.
sentences.zh: 我得告诉你，从这一集一开始，当你做“快速事实”环节时，我就确信你的其中一个“快速事实”会是迈尔斯·麦克纳特对这一集的评价。

sentences.en: But I have been waiting this whole episode.
sentences.zh: 但我整集都在等着听呢。

sentences.en: I can't wait to hear.
sentences.zh: 我迫不及待想听听了。

sentences.en: It was going to be.
sentences.zh: 本来确实会有的。

sentences.en: It was.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But then yesterday, you asked me if you could have Fast Facts number three, so I had to move this information to the end of the episode.
sentences.zh: 但昨天你问我能不能讲第三条“快速事实”，所以我不得不把这段信息移到这集最后。

sentences.en: But I was not going to leave you hanging.
sentences.zh: 但我不会让你空等。

sentences.en: Trust me.
sentences.zh: 相信我。

sentences.en: Miles McNutt gave it a B minus.
sentences.zh: 迈尔斯·麦克纳特给了它B减。

sentences.en: B minus.
sentences.zh: B减。

sentences.en: He said he really liked the cold open and the closing song.
sentences.zh: 他说他真的很喜欢开场戏和片尾曲。

sentences.en: But a lot of his review focused on comparing the two Dundee episodes.
sentences.zh: 但他评论的重点大多放在对比两集“邓迪奖”上。

sentences.en: And he felt that the first one was superior.
sentences.zh: 他觉得第一集更胜一筹。

sentences.en: And it was very hard to live in its shadow, in Miles's estimation.
sentences.zh: 在迈尔斯看来，这一集很难走出前作的阴影。

sentences.en: Miles, so much more is happening in this episode than in the first Dundees.
sentences.zh: 迈尔斯，这一集发生的事情比第一集“邓迪奖”多得多。

sentences.en: Your lead character is leaving the show.
sentences.zh: 你的主角都要离开剧组了。

sentences.en: You have a lot of ground to cover.
sentences.zh: 你要处理的事情太多了。

sentences.en: Miles, I think you're being too harsh.
sentences.zh: 迈尔斯，我觉得你太苛刻了。

sentences.en: I will end this with a letter from Autumn B.
sentences.zh: 最后我要读一封来自威斯康星州奥特姆·B的信，

sentences.en: in Wisconsin, who said,
sentences.zh: 她说，

sentences.en: Incredible women of office, ladies.
sentences.zh: 办公室里了不起的女性们，女士们。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们。

sentences.en: Thank you, Autumn.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，奥特姆。

sentences.en: After watching Michael's last Dundees, I watched the first one.
sentences.zh: 看完迈克尔最后一届“邓迪奖”后，我又看了第一届。

sentences.en: Please, please do this.
sentences.zh: 求求你们，一定要这么做。

sentences.en: Watching these two episodes back to back illuminates the evolution of Michael Scott.
sentences.zh: 连着看这两集，就能看清迈克尔·斯科特的成长轨迹。

sentences.en: A man yearning for belonging and acceptance becomes a man who has found his place, his confidence, his people, and his purpose.
sentences.zh: 一个渴望归属感和认可的人，最终成为了一个找到了位置、自信、伙伴和人生目标的人。

sentences.en: The contrast between the first and the last Dundees brings hope and comfort to all of us who believe that with time and conviction,
sentences.zh: 第一届和最后一届“邓迪奖”之间的对比，给所有相信只要有时间和信念的人带来了希望和慰藉，

sentences.en: we will become better versions of ourselves and live our best lives.
sentences.zh: 我们终将成为更好的自己，过上最精彩的生活。

sentences.en: Of all people, it was Michael Scott who would have thought, take that, Miles McNutt.
sentences.zh: 谁能想到，竟然是迈克尔·斯科特做到了，迈尔斯·麦克纳特，你看着吧。

sentences.en: That's what I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 我就是这个意思。

sentences.en: Go on them.
sentences.zh: 继续说。

sentences.en: I think you cannot compare one Dundees to another.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你不能把两届“邓迪奖”拿来比较。

sentences.en: You have to put them together.
sentences.zh: 你得把它们放在一起看。

sentences.en: Marry them.
sentences.zh: 让它们结合起来。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Watch them together.
sentences.zh: 一起看它们。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And there you have your A plus.
sentences.zh: 这样你就能给它们打A加了。

sentences.zh: 放下笔（结束发言）。

sentences.zh: 各位，这就是迈克尔最后一届“邓迪奖”了。

sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.zh: 谢谢山姆、卡西和安吉拉，我们自己的迈克尔·斯科特。
